newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, investors square positions.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, investors square positions.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Friday after a week of strong price gains.

Prices surged early in busy trade on the back of a large lift in U.S. Treasuries after the release of lower-than-expected August consumer prices. But after the gains amassed in recent sessions, prices settled lower on profit-taking.
"Investors squared positions in the afternoon," said a trader at a large Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.05 to 118.10. A week ago the bond was at 116.90.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional 2 due 2007 rose $0.30 to 100.90.

Even though the market did not sustain its initial jump Friday, traders said sentiment remained upbeat both because of the subdued inflation out of the U.S. which raised hopes of stable U.S. rates and on rising hopes that the government's economic plans will soon be passed in full by lawmakers.
News late Friday that the International Monetary Fund supports the basic elements of Argentina's new economic program underlined the support for government policy.

"(The revised program) includes important measures in the structural reform area that will help to strengthen the ongoing recovery of economic activity and employment," the IMF said in a news release quoting Managing Director Michel Camdessus.

Traders said one of the reasons the market gave up its gains in the afternoon was that the FRB ran into resistance at the 83 level. Another push next week will be needed to heave the market above that level.

Next week, the market is likely to concentrate yet again on the government's economic measures with Congress due to discuss the proposed tax increases that failed to be passed this week. Also, government proposals to reform the labor market are due to be debated next week.
